atoms.a: In early AD 878, the King of Wessex, Alfred the Great, had lost a battle against the Vikings, but he quickly recovered. What do you think he did next?

feedback.end: Alfred’s army went on to defeat the Viking leader, Guthrum, at the Battle of Edington in May AD 878.

instruction.text: Listen and select the correct answer.

atoms.a: After defeating Guthrum, Alfred forced him to sign a treaty. What do you think this treaty said?

b.sound: Guthrum had to be baptised as a Christian and retreat to East Anglia.
Guthrum was allowed to take over the entire country.

feedback.end: Peace didn’t last long though. Guthrum attacked once more and lost again. Another treaty between the two was created.

atoms.b: In this treaty, land was divided between Alfred and the Vikings. Alfred kept ((++Wessex Essex)) and the south-western half of Mercia.
The Vikings controlled Northumbria, East Anglia and the other half of ((Wessex ++Mercia)). This Viking area was known as the Danelaw.

instruction.text: Why might Alfred have allowed the Vikings to control so much land even though he defeated them?

trainers.hint: More than one answer can be correct.

feedback.end: Alfred knew that the Vikings were still strong warriors who could attack again. By giving them land, he hoped to keep the peace.

b: ++He wanted the Vikings to trust him.
He didn’t care about the land.

instruction.text: Select the boat with people on it.

feedback.end: Despite the treaty, Alfred still feared another Viking attack, so he improved Anglo-Saxon battle methods and built longships to fight at sea.

atoms.a: King Alfred improved education after the Vikings had ...
atoms.b: destroyed the monasteries where people used to be taught.
atoms.sound: King Alfred improved education after the Vikings had destroyed the monasteries where people used to be taught.

atoms.a: He had books translated from Latin so that ...
atoms.b: bishops could use them to teach people.
atoms.sound: He had books translated from Latin so that bishops could use them to teach people.

atoms.a: He also set up his own school and ordered the ...
atoms.b: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle to be written about the history of the Anglo-Saxons.
atoms.sound: He also set up his own school and ordered the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle to be written about the history of the Anglo-Saxons.

instruction.text: After his death, Alfred was given the nickname Alfred the Great. Why do you think he was given this nickname?

feedback.end: King Alfred earned his nickname by defeating the Vikings in important battles, negotiating peace and helping the English people.
